blueprint.title: Persistent Negative Self-Interpretation
blueprint.presenting_problem: Alex, a 32-year-old graphic designer, presents with persistent low mood, anhedonia, and overwhelming self-critical thoughts that have intensified over the past six months following the end of a long-term relationship. They report consistently interpreting personal experiences and interactions in a negative light, often blaming themselves for perceived failures or feeling profoundly inadequate. This pattern has led to significant social withdrawal, reduced engagement in previously enjoyed creative activities, and a pervasive sense of hopelessness about their future and relationships. Alex frequently ruminates on past mistakes and anticipates negative outcomes in social and professional contexts.
beliefs: I am fundamentally flawed and unlovable.
If I make a mistake, it proves I'm incompetent and unworthy.
Others are constantly judging my performance and finding me lacking.
My ex-partner left because I wasn't good enough, confirming my deepest fears.
There's no point in trying new things; I'll just fail or disappoint people anyway.
I always mess things up, no matter how hard I try.
No one truly cares about me; they just tolerate me.
I should be able to handle this on my own, but I can't, which makes me even more of a failure.
blueprint.therapy_frame: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), focusing on identifying and challenging negative automatic thoughts and cognitive distortions (e.g., all-or-nothing thinking, personalization, mental filter). The approach will also explore underlying core beliefs about self-worth and competence, aiming to develop more balanced and realistic interpretations of self, others, and future events. Behavioral activation strategies will be integrated to address anhedonia and social withdrawal.

blueprint.title: 社交场合的灾难性预测与回避
blueprint.presenting_problem: 李伟，28岁，软件工程师。他因严重的社交焦虑寻求咨询，尤其是在需要与新同事互动、参加团队会议或进行客户演示时。他报告说，在这些场合，他会不由自主地预测最坏的结果（例如，他会说错话、表现得很笨拙、被嘲笑或被认为能力不足）。他经常将中性的社交线索（如同事的短暂沉默或一个不经意的眼神）解读为负面评价的证据。这种焦虑导致他频繁回避社交活动，即使是公司内部的非正式聚会也尽量不参加。他感到自己的职业发展受到阻碍，人际关系也因此变得紧张。他渴望能够更自在地与人交流，但又深陷于对负面评价的恐惧中。
beliefs: 我必须在所有社交场合都表现得完美无缺，否则我就会被评判和排斥。
如果我犯了哪怕一点小错，那都会被无限放大，成为别人嘲笑我的把柄。
我的想法和感受是不重要的，或者说出来会显得我很愚蠢。
别人总是比我更自信、更受欢迎，我永远也达不到他们的水平。
我其实很努力，在专业领域也很有能力，但这些在社交上似乎毫无用处。
也许我只是想太多了，但这种想法我控制不住。
如果我能完全避免社交，我就不会感到焦虑了。
blueprint.therapy_frame: 本案例将采用认知行为疗法（CBT），特别是基于贝克（Beck）模型的认知重构技术。治疗将侧重于识别李伟在社交情境中的自动化负面思维和灾难性预测，挑战这些思维的合理性，并帮助他发展更现实、更适应性的认知替代。通过行为实验和暴露练习，逐步帮助他面对和减少对社交情境的恐惧和回避行为。同时，也会探讨其核心信念（如对完美主义和负面评价的恐惧）的形成和影响。
